mapping_basis: The kit maps the name DNp17 and line SS02553 to two MANC types, DNp17 and DNut046. The paper's anatomy (6 neurons per hemisphere; lower tectulum, haltere and neck neuropils) does not pick one, so UNMAPPED per section 4.
n_flies_note: about 7 DNp17-without-DopaMeander flies read from Fig. 3E; 26 flies in total, most selected for a visible walking phenotype
notes: Authors conclude DNp17 increases walking 'only slightly, if at all'. Flies were partly pre-selected for walking phenotype, and other non-DN types may have been co-labelled. Leg fields unclear because effect is marginal and only centroid speed was measured.
other_cell_types: variable subsets of the other SS02553 cell types (local brain interneurons types 3,4,7; ascending neurons types 5,8; VNC local type 6), excluding DopaMeander
penetrance: small speed increase (roughly 2-3 mm/s from Fig. 3E), significantly less than DopaMeander+DNp17 flies (p=0.006)
quote: we used a stochastic labeling approach to show that DNp17 increases walking speed only slightly, if at all
sensory_condition: individual flies in UFO arena
source_locator: Fig. 3D-F (DNp17>CsChr without DopaMeander, blue); Discussion 'DNp17 is unlikely to drive fast forward walking'
stimulation: 625 nm LED ring, 4.07 mW/cm2, 10 s pulses, 9 trials

notes: ABSTRACT ONLY. The hypothesis the unilateral experiments support is stated in the abstract: 'turning while walking backward might reflect asymmetric activation of the left and right MDNs'. So the coded outcome is backward walking with turning (walking convention -> all legs yes). The effector, stimulation, preparation, sex and driver line are not in the abstract. effector_kind='optogenetic' is a PLACEHOLDER forced by the schema enum (no unknown value) and is not supported by the source. preparation='other' means unknown. Needs full-text verification. The abstract's sentence that MDN activity is 'sufficient to trigger backward walking [19]' cites earlier work (ref 19), so no record was written for it here.
